title: DSL Art. 21 Important Data Catalogue freshness, classification coverage, and sectoral Important Data List alignment tracker
exclusions: Excludes datasets that have been formally exempted by the sectoral protection department in writing or that fall below the operator's documented General Data threshold (per the operator's classification policy).
evidence: Saved search `UC-22.61.5` archived daily to `audit_evidence` with `cn_csl_clause="DSL-Art-21"` and `data_tier`. Every row pins (dataset_id, dataset_name, business_unit, data_tier, sectoral_list_alignment, last_classification_date, days_since_classification, owner, risk_score).

compliance.assurance_rationale: DSL Art. 21 establishes the data-classification regime (General Data / Important Data / Core Data), requires every region and department to compile an Important Data Catalogue, and requires operators of Important Data to perform risk assessment and maintain protection corresponding to the data tier. The Important Data Catalogue is the foundational operator-side evidence required by sectoral inspectors; this UC tracks its completeness, freshness, and alignment with the published sectoral Important Data List.
compliance.controlObjective: Demonstrates that every dataset is classified, the Important Data Catalogue is fresh, and the operator's catalogue is aligned to the latest sectoral Important Data List.
compliance.evidenceArtifact: Saved search archived to `audit_evidence`, the `Important Data Catalogue` dashboard, the sectoral Important Data List of record, the Personal Information Impact Assessment register (UC-22.61.8).

controlTest.positiveScenario: UC-22.61.5 positive (DSL, Art., Important, Data, Catalogue): ingest synthetic events into `index=target_index` sourcetype='target_sourcetype' where `count` grouped by `entity` satisfies `days_since_classification` > 365, or `risk_score` > 0 for 'DSL Art. 21 Important Data Catalogue freshness, classification coverage, and sectoral Important Data List alignment tracker'. Validate lookup `cn_sectoral_important_data_list`. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row.
controlTest.negativeScenario: UC-22.61.5 negative (alignment tracker): ingest benign `target_index` / `target_sourcetype` events where `entity` stays below `days_since_classification` > 365, or `risk_score` > 0, or exclude the test entity via `compliance_exception_register.csv`. Variant 0 confirms zero alert rows for 'DSL Art. 21 Important Data Catalogue freshness, classification coverage, and sectoral Important Data List alignment tracker'.

dataSources: KV Store `cn_important_data_catalog_lookup` (dataset_id, dataset_name, business_unit, hosting_region, data_tier, sectoral_list_ref, last_classification_date, classifier_id, owner, project_status). KV Store `cn_sectoral_important_data_list` (sectoral_list_ref, list_version, effective_date, list_categories). ServiceNow CMDB (`snow:cmdb_ci`) for dataset inventory reconciliation.
app: Splunk Enterprise Security (Splunkbase 263), Splunk Add-on for ServiceNow (Splunkbase 1928), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (Splunkbase 1621).
spl:
| inputlookup cn_important_data_catalog_lookup
| eval now_ts = now()
| eval days_since_classification = if(isnotnull(last_classification_date), round((now_ts - last_classification_date) / 86400, 1), null())
| lookup cn_sectoral_important_data_list sectoral_list_ref OUTPUT list_version effective_date
| eval list_stale = if(isnotnull(effective_date) AND (now_ts - effective_date) > (365 * 86400), 1, 0)
| eval classification_missing = if(isnull(last_classification_date) OR isnull(data_tier), 1, 0)
| eval classification_stale = if(isnotnull(days_since_classification) AND days_since_classification > 365, 1, 0)
| eval important_or_core = if(data_tier IN ("Important Data","Core Data"), 1, 0)
| eval sectoral_alignment_missing = if(important_or_core = 1 AND isnull(sectoral_list_ref), 1, 0)
| eval risk_score = case(
    classification_missing = 1, 80,
    sectoral_alignment_missing = 1 AND data_tier = "Core Data", 95,
    sectoral_alignment_missing = 1, 75,
    classification_stale = 1 AND important_or_core = 1, 70,
    classification_stale = 1, 40,
    list_stale = 1 AND important_or_core = 1, 50,
    1=1, 0)
| where risk_score > 0
| sort 0 -risk_score, +days_since_classification
| table dataset_id dataset_name business_unit data_tier sectoral_list_ref last_classification_date days_since_classification classification_missing classification_stale sectoral_alignment_missing list_stale risk_score
description: Alerts on 'DSL Art. 21 Important Data Catalogue freshness, classification coverage, and sectoral Important Data List alignment tracker' (UC-22.61.5) using `index=target_index` sourcetype `configured sourcetype` via lookup `cn_sectoral_important_data_list` by aggregating `count` grouped by `entity` over `the scheduled window` and alerting when `days_since_classification` > 365, or `risk_score` > 0. Keywords: DSL, Art., Important, Data, Catalogue. Focuses on alignment tracker behaviour so compliance teams can triage UC-22.61.5 without ad-hoc log review.
value: UC-22.61.5 accelerates insight into alignment tracker ('DSL Art. 21 Important Data Catalogue freshness, classification coverage, and sectoral Important Data List alignment tracker') by tracking `activity` on lookup `cn_sectoral_important_data_list`, reducing audit findings, regulatory gaps, and attestation delays before spreadsheet checks hide regressions.
implementation: (1) Populate `cn_important_data_catalog_lookup` from the existing data-catalogue tool (Microsoft Purview, Collibra, Alation, BigID, OneTrust) extended with the four DSL tiers. (2) Maintain `cn_sectoral_important_data_list` against the current sectoral Important Data List publication. Reload every 90 days or on regulator update. (3) The DPO + sectoral compliance lead reviews each Important / Core classification quarterly. (4) Schedule UC-22.61.5 daily at 06:00 Beijing time; route `risk_score >= 70` to the DPO + Business Unit Owner at severity P2.
visualization: (Panel 1) Datasets by tier (General / Important / Core / Sectoral). (Panel 2) Classification freshness heat map. (Panel 3) Sectoral-list alignment gaps. (Panel 4) Important Data Catalogue trend (12 months).

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Authorised CN CSL control testing** — Internal audit exercises 'DSL Art. 21 Important Data Catalogue freshness, classification coverage, and sectoral Important Data List alignment tracker' (UC-22.61.5) on `entity` during scheduled clause DSL-Art-21 sampling. Match compliance programme calendar.

2. **External assessor sampling** — QSA activity spikes `index=audit_evidence` `configured sourcetype` without crossing `days_since_classification` > 365. Cross-check engagement letter in `cn_csl_exception_register.csv`.

3. **Planned maintenance affecting control telemetry** — CAB change pauses ingestion to `audit_evidence` for `entity`. Compare `_time` with active change record.

4. **Third-party processor under contract** — BAA/DPA-covered vendor generates expected rows grouped by `entity` during normal service delivery.

**Suppression mechanism:** `cn_csl_exception_register.csv` keyed on `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`, joined before alert threshold.
reviewer: PRC Data Security SME Panel + DPO + Business Unit Data Stewards
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

- Splunk Enterprise >= 9.2 or Splunk Cloud (PRC region for in-PRC datasets).
- A data-catalogue platform with API export (Microsoft Purview, Collibra, Alation, BigID, OneTrust).
- KV Store `cn_important_data_catalog_lookup` seeded daily from the data-catalogue API.
- KV Store `cn_sectoral_important_data_list` curated quarterly from sectoral publications.

## Step 1 - Catalogue KV Stores

```ini
[cn_important_data_catalog_lookup]
enforceTypes = true
field.dataset_id = string
field.dataset_name = string
field.business_unit = string
field.hosting_region = string
field.data_tier = string
field.sectoral_list_ref = string
field.last_classification_date = time
field.classifier_id = string
field.owner = string
field.project_status = string

[cn_sectoral_important_data_list]
enforceTypes = true
field.sectoral_list_ref = string
field.sectoral_department = string
field.list_version = string
field.effective_date = time
field.list_categories = string
```

## Step 2 - Schedule

```ini
[UC-22.61.5: DSL Important Data Catalogue Freshness]
cron_schedule = 0 6 * * *
dispatch.earliest_time = -1d@d
dispatch.latest_time = now
actions = summary_index, notable
action.summary_index._name = audit_evidence
action.summary_index.marker = uc=22.61.5,reg=CN-CSL,clause=DSL-Art-21,tier=$data_tier$
alert.severity = 4
```

## Step 3 - Runbooks

**`risk_score >= 80`** (owner: DPO, severity P2): Within 5 business days, complete classification of the dataset and align to the sectoral list.

**`risk_score 40-79`** (owner: Business Unit Data Steward, severity P3): Within 10 business days, refresh classification and confirm sectoral-list alignment.

## Step 4 - Sectoral-specific notes

- **Automotive**: 2021 Provisions on Automotive Data Security Management list six categories of Important Data — military / state-organ surveys, geographic data including >10cm-precision images, road-vehicle flows including continuous-tracking, intersection / parking-lot CCTV >100 cameras, etc.
- **Industrial / MIIT**: 2020 Industrial Data Classification and Grading Guide defines five-grade severity classification specific to industrial sectors.
- **Telecom / MIIT**: industrial-internet sector list updates 2022-2024; track quarterly.
- **Finance / CBIRC**: banking sector data-classification guidelines (JR/T 0197-2020).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Splunk Enterprise Security (Splunkbase 263), Splunk Add-on for ServiceNow (Splunkbase 1928), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (Splunkbase 1621).). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into index=main. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`classification_missing, classification_stale, days_since_classification, important_or_core`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: China divides company data into important, very-important, and regular tiers. Each year the government can update which data is in which tier. We make sure every dataset has the right tier label and the labels are fresh.
